Plucked acoustic guitar and pizzicato strings, a little glockenspiel, soft flute and clarinet, light hand percussion. 92 BPM, playful and warm, like a sunny alpine meadow, unobtrusive under a narrator. lines.text: [warm] Meet the marmot: a squirrel, believe it or not, and the heaviest kind there is.
Fifteen species live across the mountains and meadows of Europe, Asia and North America.
A lookout stands tall and whistles. One whistle can mean an eagle; a string of them, a fox.
Families share a burrow, and greet each other nose to nose. [softly] Yes, it's as cute as it sounds.
All summer long they eat grasses, herbs and flowers, fattening up for winter.
Then they hibernate, for up to nine months, their hearts slowing to about five beats a minute.
They sleep in a family pile, and bigger huddles are more likely to make it to spring.
The groundhog is a marmot too. Every February second, Punxsutawney Phil forecasts the spring.
Their whistles even named a ski town: Whistler, in British Columbia, after the hoary marmot.
In two thousand three, fewer than thirty Vancouver Island marmots were left in the wild. [pause] Now there are more than four hundred.
[upbeat] Every frame of this film is code: Tabbied patterns, rendered with Remotion.
